title: Supervisor health dashboard missing last_refresh marker (#8)
body:
## Premise

The dashboard body at #8 does not contain a `last_refresh: <ISO8601>` marker. Either the dashboard has never been rebuilt by the current version of `stats-health-dashboard.sh`, or the marker has been stripped from the body.

## Why this matters

The supervisor health dashboard is the framework's primary single-glance health surface. When it stops refreshing, operators keep trusting green numbers that no longer reflect reality — every decision derived from "dashboard says green" becomes invalid.

## Triage

1. Inspect the stats scheduler status (macOS):

   ```bash
   launchctl list | grep -i aidevops-stats-wrapper
   tail -40 ~/.aidevops/logs/stats.log
   ls -la ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.aidevops.aidevops-stats-wrapper.plist
   ```

2. Run the refresh manually and capture the error:

   ```bash
   bash ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/stats-wrapper.sh 2>&1 | tail -40
   ```

3. Check the dashboard issue directly:

   ```bash
   gh api repos/Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-ai-plugin-translations/issues/8 --jq '{updated_at, body_length: (.body|length)}'
   ```

## Remediation

- **Missing plist:** re-run `setup.sh --non-interactive` (or `aidevops update`) with PULSE_ENABLED=true so `setup_stats_wrapper` reinstalls `com.aidevops.aidevops-stats-wrapper.plist`.
- **`set -euo pipefail` fail:** the post-t2418 wrapper emits `HEALTH-DASHBOARD-FAIL exit=<N>` on error. Grep `stats.log` on that prefix.
- **Body size / API error:** inspect `stats.log` — look at `gh` HTTP errors and `_update_health_issue_for_repo` failures.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Root cause identified and documented on this issue.
- [ ] `gh issue view 8 --repo Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-ai-plugin-translations` shows an update within 24h of closing this alert.
- [ ] `last_refresh:` marker is present in the dashboard body.

body:

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `WordPress core translation client server` -> 0 hits; no relevant lessons.
- [x] Discovery pass: 0 target-file commits in the local last-48h view, 0 open matching PRs, and 0 matching implementation issues.
- [x] File refs verified: manager, API client, admin settings, entrypoint, README, and readme confirmed on GitHub `main`.
- [x] Tier: `tier:thinking`; completeness discovery, multi-domain package handling, rolling compatibility, and safe precedence need architectural reasoning.
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision: skipped pending the server contract in the linked dependency.

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-09-13
- **Session:** OpenCode interactive
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Blocked by:** `Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-ai-translation-server#24`
- **Conversation context:** The client scans and installs plugin translations only. It must also fill missing WordPress core strings for incomplete locales.

## What

Add WordPress core language-pack discovery, asynchronous request/check, installation, lifecycle accounting, and status reporting. Consume the typed/versioned core contract delivered by the server dependency. Request AI work only for missing core strings, install packages through the native core language-pack path, and keep official human translations authoritative.

## Why

The current refresh enumerates plugins, queries `wp_get_installed_translations("plugins")`, accepts only `translations_api` type `plugins`, creates updater objects with type `plugin`, and stores files under plugin assumptions. As a result, incomplete WordPress core locales receive no AI gap-fill.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:thinking`

**Tier rationale:** WordPress core uses versioned, multi-domain language packs and differs from plugin slug/textdomain/install conventions. The worker must validate native behavior and coordinate a rolling client/server contract without risking official files.

## Seeded Draft PR

- **Decision:** Skipped
- **Rationale:** Do not anchor client code before server issue #24 documents the accepted payload and package metadata.
- **Status:** `blocked`
- **Freshness evidence:** Current GitHub main paths and repository issue/PR state checked on 2026-09-13.
- **Verification run:** Research only.
- **Stale-assumption warning:** Refresh main and inspect the merged server contract before implementation.

## How (Approach)

### Progressive Context Plan

- **Read first:** Core refresh, API, install, completeness, cache, and cleanup methods in `src/class-translation-manager.php`; batch request in `src/class-translation-api-client.php`.
- **Load only if:** `src/class-admin-settings.php`, the entrypoint, and docs once state/UX fields are known.
- **Why:** Separate generic target lifecycle from plugin-specific assumptions without expanding synchronous request work.
- **Stop when:** Server contract, core-domain completeness source, native updater object, ledger key, rollback, and E2E check are explicit.

### Worker Quick-Start

- Keep network/API work off `translations_api`; current behavior schedules cron and serves cached results.
- Core identity must include exact WordPress version and locale. Do not model core as plugin slug/textdomain.
- Validate `translations_api("core", ...)`, `wp_get_installed_translations("core")`, `wp_get_translation_updates()`, and `Language_Pack_Upgrader` object/package behavior against the installed WordPress version.
- Core includes multiple domains/files. Never use one local PO percentage as proof that all core strings are complete.
- Preserve official translations and never delete/overwrite core files outside a verified package transaction.

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: src/class-translation-api-client.php` - send/parse the documented typed core batch contract with old-server fallback.
- `EDIT: src/class-translation-manager.php` - discover, queue, cache, install, ledger, and safely clean core packs.
- `EDIT: src/class-admin-settings.php` - distinguish core and plugin coverage/activity.
- `EDIT: superdav-ai-language-packs.php` - lifecycle cleanup/version wiring if new core state is added.
- `EDIT: README.md` and `readme.txt` - feature, privacy payload, compatibility, and operating behavior.
- `EDIT: src/phpstan-bootstrap.php` only if new bootstrap symbols require it.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `translations_api` filter, cron refresh, profile-locale jobs, admin status readers, and WordPress language-pack updater.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** Site transients/options for refresh state/cache/ledger/stats and `Language_Pack_Upgrader` writes under `WP_LANG_DIR`.
- **Existing verification/tests:** No tracked test suite found. Use PHP syntax, Composer PHPStan, WP-CLI activation, REST/core update checks, and real string loading in the shared WordPress install.
- **Schemas/config:** No database schema; serialized options/transients need backward-compatible migration/default handling.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** Downloaded core packages and WordPress language files, including any `.mo`, `.po`, `.l10n.php`, or JSON files in the server contract.
- **Migrations/backfills:** Existing plugin cache/state/ledger entries remain readable; add type/version to new identity without losing old entries.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** Deactivation and stale cleanup may clear plugin-owned state but must never broadly remove official/core files. Rollback disables core requests while preserving valid installed packs.

### Implementation Steps

1. Wait for server issue #24 to define and merge the core request/result/package contract. Record the minimum server capability/fallback signal.
2. Inspect native WordPress core translation update shapes and files in the shared dev install. Decide how to determine whether a locale has missing core strings without falsely treating a present package as 100% complete.
3. Refactor request/cache parsing enough to accept typed core results while preserving plugin payloads and legacy result keys. Old servers must fail softly and retry later, not produce admin fatals or malformed plugin jobs.
4. Extend the asynchronous refresh state machine with a bounded/idempotent core phase for every detected non-English locale and exact `get_bloginfo("version")`. Preserve chunk resume and pending semantics.
5. Build native core updater entries from validated server metadata and install through `Language_Pack_Upgrader`. Verify each expected core domain loads and human translations retain precedence.
6. Make cache and persistent ledger identity type/version/locale aware. Update stats/status copy to report core separately without inflating plugin counts.
7. Update cleanup/deactivation and docs. Exercise plugin-only, 100%-complete core, incomplete core, server unavailable, interrupted cron, WordPress upgrade, and multisite/user-locale paths.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** Cron resume and locale hooks can overlap; deduplicate core/version/locale requests and avoid partial cache publication.
- **Migration/rollback:** Deserialize old plugin-only state safely. Never mass-delete root core language files during rollback.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** New client against old server must soft-fail core only; old client behavior and plugin translation results remain unchanged.
- **Idempotency/retry:** Repeated scans and resumed cron events must not reinstall or recount identical core packages indefinitely.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** A failed core request/install leaves prior official and AI packs usable, records pending/error state safely, and retries without blocking plugin scans.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
php -l superdav-ai-language-packs.php
php -l src/class-translation-api-client.php
php -l src/class-translation-manager.php
php -l src/class-admin-settings.php
composer validate --no-check-publish
composer phpstan
wp plugin activate superdav-ai-language-packs
wp cron event run sd_ai_lang_packs_refresh_cache
wp language core list --format=json

```

- **Surface mapping:** Syntax/PHPStan cover changed PHP and serialized-shape consumers; activation/cron/core-language commands cover lifecycle and native installation. Add a REST fixture/check against the merged server and load representative front-end/admin/network-admin strings.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Required because refresh state, API compatibility, filesystem packages, multisite locales, and public docs all change.
- **Broad verification command:** Repository-required gate at refreshed HEAD plus end-to-end incomplete-core installation and plugin regression scan.

### Recoverability Checkpoint

- [ ] Focused API fallback, cron resume, and core installation checks pass.
- [ ] WIP commit created before broad gates: `wip: add WordPress core language-pack support`.
- [ ] Full plugin/core compatibility and static checks then run.

### Safety-Stop Recovery

- **Original objective:** Fill missing WordPress core translations safely.
- **Preserved user directions:** Thinking tier and auto dispatch.
- **Trigger and evidence:** server dependency is pending.
- **Completed and verified:** Client architecture mapped; no code changed.
- **Remaining acceptance criteria:** All criteria below.
- **Unsafe route not to repeat:** Do not guess the server contract or delete core language files broadly.
- **Next safe route:** Resume from the merged server contract and native WordPress fixtures.
- **Resume condition:** Server issue #24 contract is merged and package installation proven.
- **Owner and status:** Dispatched worker; blocked.

### Files Scope

- `src/class-translation-api-client.php`
- `src/class-translation-manager.php`
- `src/class-admin-settings.php`
- `src/phpstan-bootstrap.php`
- `superdav-ai-language-packs.php`
- `README.md`
- `readme.txt`
- `tests/**` only for a focused existing or justified test surface

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Each detected non-English locale is checked asynchronously for exact-version core gaps through the server core contract.
- [ ] A returned core package installs through native WordPress language-pack machinery and representative default/admin/network-admin strings load.
- [ ] A 100%-complete official locale triggers no AI package generation or replacement.
- [ ] Existing non-empty human translations remain authoritative after AI gap-fill installation.
- [ ] Plugin scanning, result parsing, installation, counts, user-locale requests, and cleanup remain unchanged.
- [ ] New client against an old/unavailable server fails softly for core, preserves cached/plugin results, and retries later.
- [ ] Refresh resume, ledger identity, status counts, and cleanup distinguish target type/version/locale without corrupting old plugin-only state.
- [ ] Syntax, static analysis, cron, multisite locale, native core install/load, and plugin regression checks pass.

## Context & Decisions

- Keep all external calls asynchronous.
- Treat core as first-class and versioned.
- Human translations take precedence; AI fills gaps only.
- Do not infer complete core coverage from one installed file.
- Follow the server contract rather than inventing a second protocol.

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** `Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-ai-translation-server#24` must define and merge the typed core/package contract.
- **Blocks:** End-user WordPress core gap filling.
- **External:** WordPress core translation/update APIs and the configured translation service.

| Implementation | 4-6h | Refresh/API/install/state/status/docs |
| Verification | 2h | Core E2E, fallback, multisite, plugin regression |

title: Feature: Locale-aware custom settings and labels with cached AI Connectors translations
body:
# Feature: Locale-aware custom text with AI Connectors translation and caching

## Origin and goal

Requested by the maintainer: extend the Languages add-on beyond packaged gettext translations so a site can be fully localized, including administrator-authored text stored in settings, labels, instructions, and other customer-facing fields. Automatically translate eligible text through WordPress's AI Client / Connectors API and cache the results. This is an implementation brief, not a request for another approval round. #auto-dispatch

Target repository: `Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-language-packs`. Integrate with Ultimate Multisite and its add-ons; do not confuse this feature with the separate Language Selector add-on, which selects languages rather than translating custom text.

## Why

Language packs translate static plugin strings, but custom database values bypass gettext. For example, Ultimate Multisite's `domain_mapping_instructions` is a single network-wide textarea. Its getter reads the saved string, substitutes network placeholders, then applies `wu_get_domain_mapping_instructions`. A customer's profile language does not select a translated version of that custom string.

DNS instructions are the first end-to-end example, not the boundary of the feature. The same infrastructure must cover user-visible text inputs, textareas, rich text, custom labels, help text, notices, checkout/form copy, configured button text, and other editable text needed for a localized experience.

## Discovery and verified reference files

- Memory recall: no relevant prior lessons found.
- Repository `main` inspected at `a09256b10a3f471ee97f0dae79606b35c0ae48bb`. Recent commits and the issue list contain language-pack/core gap-fill work, not this custom-text feature. Open PR #73 concerns core language-pack integrity; preserve its changes and re-check HEAD before implementation.
- Verified existing target files: `src/class-locale-discovery.php`, `src/class-admin-settings.php`, `src/class-translation-manager.php`, `src/class-translation-api-client.php`, `superdav-ai-language-packs.php`, `composer.json`, `phpstan.neon.dist`, `DESIGN.md`, and `README.md`.
- `Locale_Discovery` already discovers user-profile and site locales. `Translation_Manager` already uses scheduled, chunked refresh work. `Translation_API_Client` talks to the language-pack server and caches responses; that package API is not the requested arbitrary custom-text AI Connectors transport.
- Verified Ultimate Multisite integration references (paths relative to that separate repository): `inc/managers/class-domain-manager.php` (`get_domain_mapping_instructions`, `wu_get_domain_mapping_instructions`); `inc/class-settings.php` (`get_setting`, `wu_get_setting`); `inc/functions/settings.php`; `inc/ui/class-domain-mapping-element.php`.
- AI reference: the inspected WordPress installation exposes `wp_ai_client_prompt()` and `wp_supports_ai()` in `wp-includes/ai-client.php`, introduced in WordPress 7.0. Confirm the implementation environment's actual versions, prompt-builder methods, provider capabilities, and error contract before coding; do not invent a REST endpoint or provider SDK method.
- New custom-string registry, translation store, AI adapter, queue, and integration adapter paths are not yet present. Choose names consistent with `src/class-*.php`, register them in the plugin bootstrap, and document the final paths.
- Tier: `tier:thinking` — cross-plugin coverage, locale/context selection, tenant isolation, and privacy boundaries require coordinated design. Draft PR skipped: issue-only handoff; no implementation or tests have been run.

## Required behavior

### 1. Registered custom-text coverage

Introduce a reusable registry/service for translatable custom strings with stable identities: owner/plugin, field key, site/network scope, rendering context, source text, source locale, and permitted output format. Expose a documented API/hooks so Ultimate Multisite add-ons, themes, and other plugins can register and resolve their custom text.

Inventory Ultimate Multisite and supported add-ons' editable user-facing text and publish a coverage matrix. Ship adapters for that inventory, including both domain-mapping and DNS-management instructions, custom checkout/form labels and descriptions, configurable notices and buttons, and supported email copy. Reuse existing filters wherever possible. Explicitly identify any surface needing a companion upstream change; do not claim unsupported third-party fields are automatically covered.

Do not indiscriminately translate every string-valued option. Exclude credentials, tokens, URLs, domains, IPs, identifiers, slugs, enum values, CSS/JS, serialized configuration, and private/customer-submitted content. Technical values inside otherwise translatable prose must remain intact. Static gettext strings continue to use normal language packs. Full localization must not be implemented by globally rewriting stored options or intercepting all option reads.

### 2. Locale selection and fallback

For authenticated interactive views, prefer the user's explicit WordPress profile language, falling back to the site's locale when the profile uses the site default. Resolve anonymous/public views using the active site language, honoring supported language-selector/multilingual integrations through a documented resolver/filter. For queued emails, capture the recipient's locale explicitly rather than using the worker's locale.

Use this deterministic fallback order: current manually supplied translation for the requested locale; valid cached AI translation for that locale; explicitly configured language-only fallback if applicable; original source text. Never show another user's language or an arbitrary available translation. Unavailable translation or AI must not prevent rendering, checkout, or domain setup.

### 3. Translation management UI

Keep original source text as the canonical value. Add an authorized translations interface alongside the existing settings/status UI, with per-field locale variants, source/translation preview, human versus AI provenance, pending/stale/failed status, edit/reset/regenerate actions, and bulk translation for selected eligible fields/locales. Preserve existing settings forms and values.

Human edits take priority and must never be silently overwritten by AI regeneration. When source text changes, mark affected translations stale; show a clear review action rather than using a translation for an unrelated source revision. Update `DESIGN.md` for new UI behavior. Support HTML only where the originating field permits it, and retain context-appropriate sanitization and escaping.

### 4. WordPress AI Connectors integration

Use the WordPress AI Client with the site's configured connector/provider and a compatible text-generation model. Do not introduce duplicate provider credentials or hard-code a vendor/model. Isolate integration behind an adapter and feature-detect API availability. Preserve the add-on's existing older WordPress/PHP compatibility and language-pack workflow; unsupported environments can use manual translations/source fallback without fatal errors.

Automatic translation is administrator-opt-in, with clear disclosure that selected custom text is sent to the configured AI provider. Offer locale selection and bounded batch/concurrency/request limits. No automatic external billing from activation alone. Translate registered eligible fields in background work when their source or target locales change; support manual bulk generation and opportunistic scheduling of cache misses without blocking page rendering. Verify whether the connector can execute unattended; providers requiring a user/browser session must report unavailable background capability and retain a safe manual/fallback path.

Treat source text as untrusted data, not instructions. Protect and validate printf placeholders, named tokens, shortcodes, HTML structure/attributes, links, domains, IP addresses, and other non-translatable tokens. Reject malformed or unsafe output; never execute returned markup/scripts or return unsanitized AI text.

### 5. Persistent translations and cache lifecycle

Persist human translations and successful generated translations as durable records; use an acceleration cache separately so eviction does not trigger paid regeneration of already stored results. Key records/lookups by tenant/network/site scope, owner and field/context, source locale, source-content hash, and target locale; track translation/prompt version and provider/model provenance.

Source edits invalidate the appropriate revision only. Provide targeted regeneration/purge, explicit retention/deletion behavior, and migration/rollback guidance. Use locks and deduplication for concurrent requests; bounded retries/backoff and short-lived negative caching for failures. Never cache a failure as a successful translation. Never mix translations across tenants/networks/sites or leak private text through a public/shared translation server. Rendering a cache hit must make zero AI calls.

## Implementation boundaries and delivery

Implement this in the Language Packs add-on, with narrow optional integration adapters. No production modifications, deployments, provider provisioning, or new paid services are authorized by this issue. Do not change network DNS or overwrite live custom instructions. Store all source text and manual translations losslessly. Deactivation restores normal source-text rendering; document uninstall and rollback behavior before introducing durable storage.

Suggested slices: registry/store and locale resolver; Ultimate Multisite adapter plus manual translation UI; AI adapter/background generation/cache management; remaining inventory adapters, documentation, and verification. If companion changes or multiple child issues are necessary, link them and keep this issue open until the declared coverage and acceptance criteria are satisfied. Do not stop at a DNS-only prototype.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Two users with different profile languages see different translations of the same saved domain-mapping instructions; site-default profiles resolve correctly.
- [ ] DNS examples preserve technical CNAME targets, IPs, links, and placeholders exactly; translated source can be edited without replacing the original.
- [ ] A documented inventory covers all supported editable user-facing settings/labels, and registration adapters support additional plugins/themes without unsafe blanket option filtering.
- [ ] Locale fallback works for anonymous/public views, unsupported locales, and recipient-specific queued email contexts.
- [ ] Admins can review/edit translations, see provenance/status, and opt into bounded automatic generation through the configured WordPress AI connector.
- [ ] Manual overrides survive regeneration, cache purge, and plugin updates; source edits mark stale translations and invalidate the correct keys.
- [ ] Repeated rendering and cache eviction reuse persisted results without additional AI calls; concurrent misses schedule one job per translation identity.
- [ ] Missing API/provider, session-only connectors, disabled AI, rate limits, malformed output, and provider errors safely fall back without breaking pages.
- [ ] HTML, placeholders, shortcodes, RTL/non-Latin text, and identical text used in different contexts are handled correctly.
- [ ] Tenant isolation, capabilities, nonces, provider-consent boundaries, and sensitive/non-translatable exclusions are verified.
- [ ] Existing core/plugin language-pack installation and official-translation precedence remain unchanged; older supported environments still load safely.

## Verification

Use an isolated local WordPress multisite and the repository's existing checks. Run PHP syntax checks on changed PHP files, `composer phpstan`, and existing applicable CI checks. Do not introduce new test infrastructure without approval.

Exercise the actual domain-mapping UI with two profile locales and a site-default profile; preview another field family (checkout labels/descriptions) to prove the architecture is reusable. Verify the translation-management UI through browser evidence, including manual edit, source change/stale status, fallback, and RTL output. Use a controlled connector/test double with a request counter to verify one generation on a miss, no calls on persisted/cache hits, deduplication, and bounded failures without live paid requests. Test separate sites/networks with identical source strings and confirm isolated results. Verify excluded secret/technical fields are never sent to AI, placeholder/HTML validation rejects bad output, deactivation restores source text, and the existing language-pack path still works. Document the commands and evidence in the PR.
